title: CSS pension after 60
body:
O.P.
I'd appreciate if someone can help me out here.
My wife receives a CSS pension as her sole income. She's not eligible for any government allowances. She's just turned 60, and received a letter from CSS advising that tax on her pension is now $0. The letter states that her new gross fortnightly pension has the following components:
- Tax-free component is $0.00 - Taxable taxed is $0.00, and - Taxable untaxed is $x (the full fortnightly pension amount she is receiving).
Have they got this right and she doesn't have to pay any tax?
What about medicare levy?
We don't want to get to July and find out we owe the ATO a lump of money!
Thanks – Chris

---- replies ----
[User #3526151851 postsgrant2bWhirlpool Enthusiast] Another_Chris writes...
She's not eligible for any government allowances. She's just turned 60
She is definitely eligible for a Seniors Card W.A . Water 25% Shire rates 25% pro rata up to $260+ (probably more now ) Drivers License 50% Cost of living Rebate ($150 ) Spectacles ($50 bi-annually ) Electricity ( approx. $360) Free Seniors travel on rail / bus / ferry
[User #401099134 postsSoulcatcherParticipant] That is right Chris. After 60 your pension is tax-free. The tax-free component is always tax-free. The taxable taxed after 60 is tax-free. The taxable untaxed is taxed at your marginal tax rate with 10% tax offset ( which should reflect on your payment slip ). For Medicare levy, if your combined income in 2015 is $34,367 (couple), no Medicare levy is payable.
[User #43189786 postsK8CanbWhirlpool Enthusiast] this post was edited
Another_Chris writes...
Have they got this right and she doesn't have to pay any tax?
In the CSS pension "taxable unfunded" amount is definitely taxable if your wife's taxable income from all sources is above $18200 (for the year 2013-14) income tax is payable at the marginal rate. However, a tax offset of 10% is allowed for CSS pension from unfunded source. You may like to take a look at this fact sheet on CSS website http://www.css.gov.au/storage/CSF21.pdf
If your wife's total taxable income from all sources is less than $18200 then CSS are right, your wife may not have to file a tax return.

[User #550467108 postsAnother_ChrisParticipant] O.P.
Thanks to all for the replies. I think I'm starting to get a handle on this.
Her gross pension is $1054.12 per fortnight, so $27407.12 pa plus about $1k in interest and dividends, so about $28400 total.
She would pay 19c for each dollar over the tax-free threshold of $18200, so 19c x $10200 = $1938 or $74.54 per fortnight.
BUT she now gets the 10% offset of $1054.12 x 10% = $105.41, so her tax liability is $74.54 minus the offset of $105.12 = zero (ATO math!)
Am I on the right track?
OK – thanks. Now I just need to get on top of the medicare liability. Our combined pre-tax income last year was about $63k. So I'm guessing that she is still liable for that, and if CSS isn't taking out any tax we'll need to set something aside for that at tax time.

[User #550467108 postsAnother_ChrisParticipant] O.P.
Interesting article, although more about the PSS scheme than the older CSS scheme that both my wife and I are in. We both opted for maximum indexed pension plus lump sum upon retiring. The lump sums went into Agest > AusSuper and are still sitting there while we see how we can live on just the CSS pensions.
Now I need to learn about the taxation that we'll be liable for on a pension drawn down on the AusSuper super account. I think all my wife's fund came from taxed contributions (some cash contributions and her CSS lump sum) so should be tax free after 60. Does that sound right?
But I think mine might include some taxable untaxed sources including salary-sacrifice contributions made during the last few years of working as well as the CSS lump sum.
Still lots to learn!
[User #607221228 postsCallMeMrVainForum Regular] Chris
You are probably overthinking this one.
Bear in mind the organisations that administer CSS, PSS as well as AusSuper which is where your lump sum is, have million+ members. So they know the tax rules better than anyone, they have to get it right, otherwise they will have many unhappy members on their hands. So any tax due on the pension or lump sum will be withheld by these organisations and passed to the ATO direct, they know the rules back to front.
Basically what I am saying is you shouldn't worry about it, CSS has told you there is no tax on your wifes pension now, and AusSuper will inform you of any tax on the lumpsum. About the only thing you might be up for is the medicare levy.
[User #699145791 postsMaxplyWhirlpool Forums Addict] Gotta love the CSS : )
By the time I retire 54/11 in 6 yrs time my max pension should be over 100k (conservative estimate), & when I hit 60 I'll only pay about 6k tax total. Sweet.
They better not change the rules : /

Mr Vain – you're probably right, but better to over-think than not think about it at all. We've been caught before with a pay centre that miscalculated the tax withheld and left us with a tax debt.
And Beaver – you're right. I wish I'd joined the PS at 18 instead of 31. When I left my first job at 28 (to go to uni after 10 years in a low paying job) nobody told me about superannuation roll-over. Opportunity missed!
